races.title: State House, District 10
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: John Bell
cands.bio: John R. Bell IV is a Republican state representative for North Carolina House District 10, which includes Wayne County. He has served since 2013 and was House Majority Leader from 2016 to 2025. He works in credit union sales and business development and founded a business development firm.
cands.gaps: The pages we could read did not show any documented actions or stated positions from John Bell on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws or abortion. His campaign site describes his school-choice and teacher-pay record only in general terms, with no specific bills or votes. We found no documented stance from him on data centers or on more development. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026, and we found no documented controversies or foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. We could not confirm where he spent his childhood beyond his high school in Duplin County. We could not find details of his credit union job or his business beyond what is in his campaign biography.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign biography calls him a native of Mount Olive, NC and a graduate of North Duplin High School and UNC Wilmington, and Ballotpedia says he lives in Goldsboro.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the NC House since 2013, as House Majority Whip (elected 2015) and then Majority Leader (2016 to 2025). He works in sales and business development at a credit union and founded the business development firm Neuse Connections, LLC.
qual.why: He has more than a decade of legislative service and nine years in chamber leadership, plus a business and finance career.
qual.label: He has more than a decade of legislative service and nine years in chamber leadership, plus a business and finance career.

cands.name: Zyaire Webb
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 10 in 2026. Wayne County native from Goldsboro, East Carolina University graduate, and a welder since age 14 who builds custom cookers and smokers. No elected office held.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as recommended by two Sway voter-guide groups: Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Tevin Davis) and Waves of Democracy (Terri Robinson).

cands.gaps: He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and his campaign site is thin. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or abortion. We found no news coverage of him and no record of past public office. His exact age and the year he moved or was raised beyond Wayne County were not stated. The campaign site does not say what he studied at East Carolina University or how long he has worked as a welder beyond "since age 14."

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he was born in Goldsboro, is a Wayne County native, and went through the public school system there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Recent East Carolina University graduate with a welding degree from Wayne Community College. He has welded since age 14 and built hundreds of handcrafted cookers, smokers and fryers. No elected office or legislative, policy or budget work is documented.
qual.why: He is a first-time candidate with no legislative or policy record. His welding work is real but unrelated to writing law and the budget, so he falls in the low band.
qual.label: He is a first-time candidate with no legislative or policy record. His welding work is real but unrelated to writing law and the budget, so he falls in the low band.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site pledges a $26,000 increase in teacher pay across the board and a total increase in education funding. It says nothing on vouchers or charters.
